correction.reason: Article.md defines ReCoN nodes as script nodes plus terminal nodes. Actuator/action affordances are terminal leaves that interact with the environment, not a third core node type.
correction.supersedes: The earlier TG26o partial wording that introduced NodeType.ACTION was a formalism error.
correction.runtime_effect: Chess move affordances remain graph leaves requested by SCRIPT nodes and returning through SUR, but their node type is TERMINAL with actuator metadata.

earlier_pragmatic_engine_failure.cause: legacy ReConEngine could confirm SCRIPT nodes after children started, before failed child terminals blocked the triplet

mate_in_2_native_attempt.blocker: fully materialized feature-terminal graph is too slow for Mate_In_2 parity using the generic FormalReConEngine all-node tick loop

next_required_work: Add an indexed native formal scheduler that still uses real graph nodes and SUB/SUR/POR/RET messages but only ticks candidate subgraphs whose before/action affordance can be requested for the current board.
Keep SCRIPT/TERMINAL node state, M3 weights, and M4 maturity on the graph; actuator affordances are terminal metadata, not a separate core type. Do not reintroduce TG26n batch scoring as runtime.
Rerun no-symmetry Mate_In_1 plus Mate_In_2 parity, then symmetry-expanded 18/23, then bounded 50x replay.
interpretation: TG26o has migrated the representation into native ReCoN graph structures and proves native Mate_In_1 parity on the curated originals. It does not yet prove Mate_In_2 native parity because the honest formal runtime is currently too slow at the materialized graph size.
